text:
A patient may need a tracheostomy when the upper airway is blocked or when a breathing tube will be needed for a long time. The opening in the neck lets air reach the lungs, lets secretions be cleared, and avoids keeping a tube through the mouth or nose. Common reasons include trauma, tumors, swelling, neurological illness that weakens breathing or swallowing, and difficulty weaning from a ventilator.
